articles.title: Password: Recover NSID and Reset Password
steps: Go to the NSID password recovery page and click "I forgot my password".
Enter your NSID and click "Continue".
Choose email, SMS, or security questions to verify your identity.
Enter the verification code or answers and submit them.
Enter and confirm a new password that meets the password requirements, then click "Reset Password".
Wait at least 15 minutes for the new password to synchronize with USask services.
Update the saved password on applicable VPN, Wi-Fi, Apple device, mail, and password-manager accounts.
notes: After a password change the client must update saved wireless networks, VPN, phone mail apps and any password manager
Synchronisation can take several minutes; a failure immediately afterwards is usually a saved old password

articles.title: Wireless: Connect to uofs-secure Network
steps: Confirmed the client's NSID was active and PAWS password was current
{options}
Selected uofs-secure from the available Wi-Fi networks
Entered the client's NSID in the format the device requires and their PAWS password
Accepted the server certificate for iseberg.usask.ca
Confirmed the connection succeeded and verified internet access

windows: Confirmed the client's NSID was active and PAWS password was current
Selected the Wi-Fi icon from the bottom right task bar
Entered the client's NSID as the username and their PAWS password, then selected OK
Confirmed the connection succeeded and verified internet access
macos: Confirmed the client's NSID was active and PAWS password was current
Selected the Wi-Fi icon from the top right menu and selected uofs-secure
Entered the client's NSID as the username and their PAWS password, then selected Join
Selected Show Certificate, checked Always trust iseberg.usask.ca and selected Continue
Had the client enter their Mac administrator username and password at the Certificate Trust Settings prompt, then selected Update Settings
Confirmed the connection succeeded and verified internet access
ios: Confirmed the client's NSID was active and PAWS password was current
Opened Settings, selected Wi-Fi and selected uofs-secure
Entered the client's NSID as the username and their PAWS password, then selected Join
Verified the server was named iseberg.usask.ca and selected Trust
Confirmed the checkmark appeared beside uofs-secure and verified internet access
android: Confirmed the client's NSID was active and PAWS password was current
Opened Settings, selected Network & Internet (or Connections), selected Wi-Fi and selected uofs-secure
Confirmed the connection succeeded and verified internet access
chromeos: Confirmed the client's NSID was active and PAWS password was current
Opened Settings, selected Network > Wi-Fi and selected uofs-secure
— Identity: client's NSID in the format abc123@usask.ca
Confirmed the connection succeeded and verified internet access
linux: Confirmed the client's NSID was active and PAWS password was current
Opened Settings, selected Network, selected Wireless and selected uofs-secure
Entered the following settings in the authentication window:
— CA Certificate: DigiCert Global Root G2
— Username: client's NSID in the format abc123@usask.ca
Confirmed the connection succeeded and verified internet access
remarkable: Confirmed the client's NSID was active and PAWS password was current
Opened the hamburger menu, selected Settings, selected Wi-Fi and selected uofs-secure

optional_steps: Removed the saved uofs-secure network and rejoined it, as the client had recently reset their password
Installed the DigiCert certificate first, as the CA certificate could not be set to Use System Certificates
notes: Username format: NSID only on Windows, macOS, iOS, Android and reMarkable; full NSID@usask.ca on ChromeOS and Linux

articles.title: Multi Factor Authentication: Set Up and Troubleshoot
steps: Reset the MFA from IAM
Signed in to the Authenticator app and linked it with PAWS
Checked everything on myprofile.usask.ca
notes: A prompt asking to check a registered device is waiting for an approval tap, not a typed code
When number matching is on, the number shown on screen is typed into the app

articles.title: Microsoft 365: Install on a Personal Device
steps: Signed in to office.com with the client's USask ID
Selected Install apps and downloaded the Microsoft 365 installer
Ran the installer and waited for the installation to finish
Opened an Office app and signed in with the client's USask ID to activate it
notes: If the browser version works but desktop applications fail, the problem is usually device registration rather than the licence

articles.title: Printing: Denied or Delayed Print Jobs
steps: Check the available print credit on the account
Check the job in the print queue for a denial reason
notes: A denied job is most often an insufficient balance rather than a printer fault

articles.title: Software: Install from the Managed Software Catalogue
steps: Open the software catalogue on the managed device
Locate the application and choose install
Wait for the installation to complete and open the application
notes: The catalogue is only available on university managed Windows devices
Off campus the device must be on the VPN for the catalogue to populate

articles.title: O365 Email: Set up USask email in Outlook on Windows
steps: Opened Outlook and entered the client's USask email address
Signed in with the client's USask credentials on the Microsoft sign-in page
Approved the MFA prompt on the client's phone
Finished the account setup and confirmed the mailbox loaded

articles.title: Apple Mail: Setup on iPhone or iPad
steps: Opened Settings > Mail > Accounts > Add Account and chose Microsoft Exchange
Entered the client's USask email address and selected Sign In
Signed in with the client's USask credentials and approved the MFA prompt
Accepted the permissions and chose Mail, Contacts and Calendars to sync
Saved the account and confirmed the mailbox loaded in the Mail app

articles.title: O365 Email: Android Phone - Set up the Gmail App
steps: Opened the Gmail app and selected Add another account
Chose Exchange and Office 365 and entered the client's USask email address
Signed in with the client's USask credentials and approved the MFA prompt
Accepted the permissions and finished the account setup
Confirmed the mailbox loaded in the Gmail app

articles.title: Virtual Private Network (VPN)
steps: Confirmed the client's NSID was active and password was current
Confirmed the client was off campus, as the VPN should not be used while connected to the campus network

Confirmed the VPN connected successfully and the client could access USask resources

articles.title: Zoom at USask - Activate Your Account
steps: Confirmed the client is a USask member and needed to opt in to Zoom
Had the client sign in to My Profile
Navigated to the Opt In Services section and clicked Edit
Enabled Zoom and clicked Save Changes

Advised the client that there is a delay of approximately 30 minutes after opting in before the account can be used, and that signing in sooner may show the error "something went wrong while you tried signing in with SSO"
Advised the client to sign in at https://usask-ca.zoom.us or through the Web Conferencing channel in PAWS, and not at zoom.us, which will return an error with USask credentials

optional_steps: Advised the client that custom permissions are not supported; each site has only two groups, Owners and Members
Advised the client that ICT does not build or maintain custom workflows or forms
Advised the client that ICT does not help format or customize sites
Advised the client that email-enabled lists and libraries are not available in SharePoint Online
Advised the client that Nintex Forms and Nintex Workflows are not available in SharePoint Online

articles.title: OneDrive: Access Denied error
steps: Confirmed the client was receiving an "Access Denied" error when opening their USask OneDrive
Located the client's account in IAM
Selected Action > Grant Support under Services > OneDrive Online
Granted the role to spo999 to re-apply the owner permissions on the client's OneDrive
Entered the reason: in order to fix permissions on user's OneDrive (SharePoint Library)
Left the expiry date as default
Confirmed the client was able to open their OneDrive without the error

articles.title: OneDrive: Saving files to USask OneDrive
steps: Went to login.microsoftonline.com and had the client sign in with their NSID@usask.ca and NSID password
Opened OneDrive to the client's University of Saskatchewan OneDrive folder
Clicked Upload, selected Files, chose the files the client wanted to upload and clicked Open
Confirmed the files uploaded successfully to the client's OneDrive
Also showed the client how to save directly from Word, Excel or PowerPoint by selecting File > Save As > OneDrive - University of Saskatchewan

articles.title: JADE: Map a drive to a departmental JADE share
steps: Confirmed the name of the client's departmental JADE share
{options}
Confirmed the client could open the share and access their files
optional_steps: Mapped a network drive on the client's computer to the share on \\jade
Mapped the drive to the department's Domain DFS root under \\usask.ca instead, as the department uses a Domain DFS root

articles.title: JADE: Add a user to a share permission group
steps: Verified the requester is authorized to request access changes for this share, and is not requesting additional access for themselves
Logged into the IAM support interface
Under the Resources tab, selected Search Resources, chose Jade as the Resource Server and searched for the share name
{options}
Clicked Add Group Members, entered the user's NSID and a reason, checked the effective and expiry dates, and clicked Add
Advised that the user may need to log off and back on to their computer before the new access takes effect
optional_steps: Clicked the Groups & Services tab and selected the share's write_access permission group
Clicked the Groups & Services tab and selected the share's read-only (_ro) read_access permission group

articles.title: JADE: Increase a share quota
steps: Verified the requester is authorized to request changes for this share
Logged into the IAM support interface
Under the Resources tab, selected Search Resources, chose Jade as the Resource Server and searched for the share name
Clicked Action > Edit next to the quota attribute
Entered a higher integer value for the quota and clicked Save
{options}
optional_steps: As the increase was beyond 1000 GB, used Assign Attributes to select quota_tb and entered the quota in TB

articles.title: JADE: Client cannot access a share
steps: Confirmed the client was logged on to their computer with an account that should have access to the share
Confirmed the client's computer was on a functional on-campus wired or wireless network
Checked whether the client could see the share by browsing to \\jade
Confirmed other JADE shares were reachable under \\jade2, \\jade3 and \\jade4, confirming the servers were up
In IAM, searched the share under Resources > Search Resources and ran a Get Info transaction to check the share's permission groups
{options}
Confirmed the client could access the share
optional_steps: Found the client was not a member of the share's permission groups
Found the client had recently been added to the group
Had the client log off and back on to their computer so the new group membership took effect

steps: Opened PAWS and logged in

articles.title: ArcGIS Pro: How to Install
steps: Confirmed the client's ArcGIS Online account was active using their USask NSID and password
Signed in to the client's ArcGIS Online organization account, clicked their username and selected My settings
Opened the Licenses tab and confirmed ArcGIS Pro was listed with the Download ArcGIS Pro link

articles.title: Class Registration: Request a class override
steps: Had the client attempt registration under Register for Classes, add the class by CRN to the summary and click Submit
Reviewed the error by hovering over "Errors Preventing Registration"
Went to the class overrides and changing audit/credit status page and clicked Request a class override
Clicked Apply for New Override and selected Registration Error as the override type
Selected the class, entered the client's reason for the override and clicked Submit Request
Confirmed the request appeared on the client's override dashboard with the status New Request
Advised the client that the request will be processed by the college or department and they will receive an email with the decision
Advised the client that if approved, they must return to the registration channel and register for the class themselves, as registration is not automatic

articles.title: Cabinet: Can't See All My Files
steps: Confirmed the client is on a USask managed Windows device using Offline Files, and that Cabinet had been marked offline because the device couldn't reach the network share at logon
{options}
Opened the client's Cabinet folder in File Explorer
Clicked the Home tab, then Easy Access > Work Online
Refreshed the window and confirmed all of the client's Cabinet files were visible
optional_steps: Confirmed the client was connected to the USask VPN, as they were off campus
Opened Control Panel > Windows Tools first, as the device runs Windows 11

articles.title: Devices: Basic Hardware Troubleshooting
steps: Confirm the device powers on and is charged
Reseat cables and try a different port or cable
Restart the device and retest
Record the model and symptoms if the problem persists
notes: Physical repair of university owned equipment is handled by a technician, not at the desk

platform_notes.note: On ChromeOS and Linux the wireless identity needs the full username with the domain, not the short username alone. This is the most common first attempt failure.
On macOS the certificate trust prompt asks for the local Mac administrator password. Clients on personally owned Macs often do not know it, which stops the connection.

After a password reset the client must update saved wireless networks, VPN, phone mail sync and any password manager. Synchronisation is not instant, so an immediate failure is usually a saved old password rather than a fault.

A message asking the client to check their registered device is waiting for an approval tap in the authenticator app, not a typed code. With number matching the number on screen is typed into the app.
When the browser version works but desktop applications fail, check the device registration rather than the user licence. This is above desk level and is escalated.
The managed software catalogue only works on university managed Windows devices and needs the VPN when off campus. It is not an option on a personal laptop.
